title: Ziebert-Aranson crawlers have a minimum motile size: at alpha=3, sigma=0.6 crawling dies below R~12; sigma=1.3, alpha=4 keeps R=8 cells crawling
summary: Fixed-size crawlers (GROW=0, the positive-control world 20261025T0641-c04-crawler-positive-control, same kick) were run for t=200 at target radius 6, 8, 10 (probe/speeds.txt, speed per 20 time units). At alpha=3, sigma=0.6 the speed decays to 0 by t~40 (R=6), ~80 (R=8) and ~160 (R=10); R=12 crawls indefinitely (17.5 body lengths in t=500). With sigma=1.3, alpha=4 an R=8 cell settles at a steady 0.95. Consequence for dividing crawlers: if division halves a cell below the threshold the daughters round up and stop (static_daughters/sheet.png: ell=14 fission world, daughters crawl at t=35-65 and are static from t~110 on). Any crawl-and-divide world has to keep daughters above the motile size, or use the stronger myosin parameters.

finding.operator: phase-field crawler (Ziebert-Aranson) with myosin terms gamma, sigma
finding.control: matched runs differing only in target radius
